# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 1, forking from seed (tau2 default airline tool surface). Reader = mid-tier
`aws/gpt-oss-120b`, so I favored deterministic code enforcement and literal, example-bearing
parameter docs.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Multi-step WRITE stall | 17 (t0), 23 (t0) | Agent does 1 write, narrates the rest, then stops → incomplete DB | BEHAVIORAL | Composite atomic-write tool (`modify_reservation`) |
| 2 | Wrong reservation/flight (stops enumerating) | 8 (t1), 17 (t1) | Agent looks up reservations one-by-one and stops early → wrong reservation/flight chosen | CAPABILITY-GAP | Loop READ tool (`get_reservations`) |
| 3 | Unauthorized ad-hoc compensation | 37 (t1) | Agent hallucinated a $116 "voucher" via `send_certificate` for a non-cancellable reservation → extra write, DB mismatch | DECISION/RULE | In-body guard on `send_certificate` (amount must be a policy multiple of 50) |
| — | Refund number miscommunicated | 11 | Agent quotes wrong refund ($1444 vs $5244); DB already matches | KNOWLEDGE (arith) | SKIPPED — no safe code lever (see below) |
| — | Agent does no write at all | 19 (t0), 40 (t0) | Single required write never issued in one trial | BEHAVIORAL | SKIPPED — likely sim-turn artifact; no bounded tool lever |
| — | Infra `###STOP###` | 22 | user-simulator artifact | — | excluded from scoring |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | in-body guard (CODE) | `tools.py::send_certificate` | Raises unless `amount` is a positive multiple of 50 — policy compensation is $100×pax or $50×pax, always a multiple of 50. Catches the hallucinated $116 voucher; general to any out-of-policy amount. | Yes — NO passing/flaky task calls `send_certificate` with a valid amount; guard fires only on invalid amounts. |
| 1 | compose / add (CODE) | `tools.py::modify_reservation` | One atomic call applies cabin/flights + baggages + passengers by delegating to the existing update primitives, so the agent can't narrate a multi-step change and skip a step. Primitives KEPT (all used by passing/flaky tasks, so none removable). | Yes — delegates to same primitive bodies; verified a single-field (baggages-only) call is byte-identical to the primitive, so even if a passing task diverts to it the DB is unchanged. |
| 2 | loop READ / add (CODE) | `tools.py::get_reservations` | Fetches details of a LIST of reservation ids in one call so the agent enumerates every reservation without stopping early; per-id error entries. Read-only. | Yes — pure read-only add; no write path touched. |

## Verify-the-fix (ran tool bodies directly on pristine AIRLINE_DB)
- send_certificate: amount=116→raise, amount=0→raise, amount=50/100/150→OK (message). Matches task 37-t1 bad value blocked; valid policy amounts pass. No passing task calls it.
- modify_reservation: FQ8APE (task 17 target) basic_economy→economy + flights + 1 passenger + 3 bags in one call → cabin=economy, npax=1 (unchanged count), bags=3, payment appended. Cabin-only path GV1N64 business→basic_economy → refund −5244 == primitive path. Baggages-only YAX4DR (task 12 style) via composite == via `update_reservation_baggages` (identical dump) → safe under diversion.
- get_reservations: passed 4 ids incl. one bad → 4 aligned results, real ones are Reservation, bad id is {'reservation_id','error'}.
- Registration: `AirlineTools(db).get_tools()` returns 16 tools incl. `get_reservations`, `modify_reservation`; module imports clean under the eval venv (py3.12).

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 4 read-only Explore subagents in parallel to diagnose trajectory groups (8; 17; 23; 11+37). A 5th (12/25/19/40) hit context limits; recovered blast-radius facts with a small JSON-extraction script instead.
- Prior iterations: none — this is iteration 1 (RUNMAP/LEDGER empty, seed only).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- Do NOT remove any update/cancel/book primitive: task 12 uses `update_reservation_baggages`, 40 uses `update_reservation_passengers`, 11/37 use `update_reservation_flights`, 25 uses `book_reservation`, 19/37 use `cancel_reservation`. Every primitive is load-bearing for a passing/flaky task.
- The send_certificate multiple-of-50 guard is a correct, general policy encoding — keep it.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- Task 11 refund-number miscommunication: purely a spoken-value check ($5244); DB already matches. No tool CODE can force the agent to SAY a number, and enriching the `Reservation` return shape carries documented risk (field-notes §2/§4: additive/return-shape changes underperformed/corrupted signal). Not worth the regression risk.
- Tasks 19/40 "no write at all" in one trial: behavioral stall with a single required write — a composite can't help a one-step action, and the cause looks like a truncated sim turn. No bounded lever.
- Task 22: infra `###STOP###` artifact, excluded from scoring.
- Did NOT add a cancellation-eligibility guard: eligibility depends on the cancellation reason (not a tool argument) and would risk flipping passing cancels (19, 37-t0) → UNBOUNDED. Left alone.
